chunks.name: More vibrant, more structured, less gray: Strato's fresh, new look is here: A page layout built on lines, not stacked surfaces
chunks.description: This is the change you'll feel the most. Page structure used to come from nested surfaces; it now comes from lines. Sidebars, detail panels, and content regions sit flush on the page background…

chunks.name: More vibrant, more structured, less gray: Strato's fresh, new look is here: More vibrant colors, cleaner grays
chunks.description: Status colors are cleaner and brighter. Success, warning, and critical are now noticeably more saturated, so a critical alert reads as urgent, at a glance, and a success state shows the confidence it…

chunks.name: More vibrant, more structured, less gray: Strato's fresh, new look is here: Fields that read as interactive
chunks.description: Fields are now outlined and bright rather than filled. An empty field reads immediately as somewhere you can enter text, and a form full of different fields feels lighter and uncrowded.

chunks.name: More vibrant, more structured, less gray: Strato's fresh, new look is here: Refreshed chart colors
chunks.description: Chart colors followed the UI refresh with the same intent: more vivid, more distinct. The sequential palettes were rebuilt using the OKLCH color system, a perceptually-uniform model where equal…

chunks.name: More vibrant, more structured, less gray: Strato's fresh, new look is here: What this means for your app
chunks.description: Nothing to migrate. The refresh ships through Strato's design tokens, so any component you already use picks it up automatically without API changes, and no breaking changes either.

chunks.name: Document
chunks.description: This API allows you to create and manage documents, as well as manage access to them.

chunks.name: Document: Access Management
chunks.description: There are 2 different permission mechanisms. Most operations involve both mechanisms.

chunks.name: Document: Endpoint Permissions
chunks.description: IAM permissions (e.g. document:documents:read) guard endpoints. If the user doesn't have the permission required by an endpoint, the request gets rejected.

chunks.name: Document: Document Permissions
chunks.description: These permissions guard individual documents. They are modelled in the service itself, independent of IAM permissions.

chunks.name: Document: Sharing
chunks.description: By default, documents are only accessible to their owner. There are 3 ways of sharing documents.

chunks.name: Document: Owner Transfer
chunks.description: Document ownership can be changed via the transferDocumentOwner operation.

chunks.name: Document: Document Locking
chunks.description: Allows you to create and manage documents, as well as manage access to your documents via shares.

chunks.name: Document: Optimistic Locking
chunks.description: Operations which modify a document generally use mandatory optimistic locking.

chunks.name: Document: Active Locking
chunks.description: In addition to the mandatory Optimistic Locking, there is optional Active Locking.

chunks.name: Document: Deletion and Restoration
chunks.description: Deleted documents are moved to the trash and permanently deleted after 30 days.

chunks.name: Document: Snapshots
chunks.description: Document snapshots allow to reset a document's content back to an earlier state.

chunks.name: Document: Snapshot Permissions
chunks.description: All users with write access to a document may list, read, create, or restore its snapshots.

chunks.name: Document: Labels
chunks.description: Labels allow the user to organize and search their documents.

chunks.name: Document: Document Identity
chunks.description: Each document is assigned a unique and immutable identifier (id) at the time of creation.

chunks.name: Document: Admin Access
chunks.description: Regular users can only access documents owned by them or shared with them.

chunks.name: Document: User Data
chunks.description: No user data like names or email addresses are stored. Instead, SSO ids are persisted.

chunks.name: Document: Favorites
chunks.description: Users can mark documents as favorites for quick access. Favorites are personal — the favorite state is per-user and is not visible to the document's owner or other users.

chunks.name: Document: System-owned Documents
chunks.description: Some documents are created and maintained by the system itself, instead of being user-owned.

chunks.name: Document: Ready-made Documents
chunks.description: Apps can contain documents which automatically become available to all users of the environment when the app gets installed or updated. The property originAppId indicates app ownership.

chunks.name: Document: Extension-shipped Documents
chunks.description: Extensions can contain documents which automatically become available to all users of the environment when the extension gets installed or updated. The property originExtensionId indicates extension…
